listenings.text: Hi Fabia, this is Karen. You asked me for the story of the firm, so here it is, in six lines. We started in 1992, with three people. We used to do everything on paper. We used to work only with Brazilian clients. In 2015 we got our first foreign client. He wanted all his reports in English. Today we have sixty people and ninety clients.

Hi Fabia, this is David. Before our meeting, let me tell you how it used to work here. One person used to run our whole payroll. Her name was Sandra. Every December she used to work both weekends. She retired in March, and we did not replace her. So today nobody here knows the process. I need a company, not one person. Can you send me your proposal by Friday?

paras: The firm opened in 1992 with three people and a filing cabinet. It used to do bookkeeping for shops and small clinics in the same neighbourhood, and it did not use to take clients from outside the city.

In 2008 the founder's daughter joined and pushed for a computer system. The transition took four years and nearly split the partnership. Two of the older partners left. The ones who stayed later said it was the decision that saved the firm.

The real shift came in 2015, with a foreign client nobody had gone looking for. They needed reports in English, on a fixed calendar, with an audit trail. The firm had outgrown its legacy system without noticing, and rebuilding it took another three years.

Today the firm employs eighty people and serves a hundred and forty companies. What the partners tell prospects is not that they are big. It is that they have changed once already, on purpose, and know exactly what it costs.
